title: Unique Email Groups
summary: Given an array of valid email addresses, normalize each by removing dots from the local name, stripping content after the first '+', converting to lowercase, and normalizing the domain name to lowercase.
statement: Given an array of valid email addresses, normalize each by removing dots from the local name, stripping content after the first '+', converting to lowercase, and normalizing the domain name to lowercase. Count the distinct groups formed by these normalized emails.
constraints: emails is a nonempty list of valid addresses with one @ separator each.
Before @, ignore dots and everything from the first + onward; lowercase both local and domain parts.
hints: Normalization must retain the boundary between local and domain parts.
Split at @, truncate the local part at +, remove its dots, lowercase both pieces, and rejoin with @.
Insert each canonical address into a set.
Two addresses share a group exactly when all normalization rules yield the same boundary-preserving canonical string.
editorial: Two addresses share a group exactly when all normalization rules yield the same boundary-preserving canonical string.

tests.explanation: The first two normalize together, while the third has another domain, giving two groups.
Lowercasing produces a@b.com, so the single address forms one group.
